bib.title: Training Neural Response Selection for Task-Oriented Dialogue Systems
bib.venue: ACL 2019 (57th Annual Meeting of the ACL), pp. 5392-5404

read.skipped: References skimmed only; no appendix in PDF; supplemental t-SNE plots not included.

question: Can a response selection model be pretrained on large general-domain conversational data (Reddit) and fine-tuned on small task-oriented dialogue domains?
hypothesis: Pretraining on Reddit then fine-tuning overcomes the low-data regime and beats training from scratch and off-the-shelf sentence encoders.
contributions: Two-step pretrain on Reddit then fine-tune training method for response selection
Comparison of FT-DIRECT and FT-MIXED fine-tuning
New e-banking FAQ dataset with 77 categories
Evaluation on diverse domains vs TF-IDF, BM25, USE, ELMo, BERT baselines

method.summary: A dual-tower (shared-weights input and response) n-gram + self-attention encoder is trained with in-batch negatives on 727M Reddit pairs, then fine-tuned on small target datasets either directly or with in-batch Reddit mixing (3:1).

datasets.name: Reddit
datasets.size: 654,396,778 train / 72,616,937 test pairs (Table 1); text says >727M pairs from ~3.7B comments Jan 2015-Dec 2018
datasets.preprocessing: lower-cased, tokenised; numbers of 5+ digits -> #; words >16 chars -> LONGWORD; <S> </S> added; comments kept only if >8 and <128 word tokens (Reddit)

models.name: Input-response encoder (Reddit model)
models.architecture: shared unigram+bigram embeddings (d=320), positional emb + self-attention (projection dim 64), sqrt-length reduction, 3 x 1024 swish layers, linear to 512; scaled cosine score
models.vocab: 105K unigrams (>=10 occurrences in 1M Reddit subset) + 200K bigrams; OOV n-grams hashed to random id 0-50,000

models.name: TARGET-ONLY
models.architecture: same encoder trained from scratch on target data

other.tuned: word embedding sizes and embedding dropout rates

models.name: USE / USE-LARGE, ELMo, BERT-SMALL, BERT-LARGE (SIM and MAP)

other.MAP: linear map W+alpha*I on response vector, trained on random 10,000 train examples with Eq.1 loss; vectors l2-normalised

training.objective: in-batch softmax over K pairs with scaled cosine score, J = sum S(xi,yi) - sum log sum_j exp S(xi,yj); label smoothing: positive gets 0.8, rest spread over in-batch negatives
training.lr_schedule: decay by 0.3x every 1M steps after the first 2.5M steps
training.regularisation: label smoothing 0.8; embedding dropout tuned for TARGET-ONLY
training.hardware: 13 GPU nodes, one Tesla K80 each

other.embedding gradients: unigram and bigram embedding gradients scaled by batch size
other.fine-tuning: early stopping on in-domain validation data; fine-tuning lr, batch size, steps not given
other.FT-MIXED: Reddit:in-domain ratio 3:1 in every batch; 3:1 to 1:3 gave slight variation

inference.decoding: rank candidates by scaled cosine similarity
inference.samples: single run per cell; no seeds reported
inference.retrieval: candidate response vectors precomputed; approximate NN search possible

metrics.name: R100@1
metrics.definition: fraction of queries whose correct response ranks first among 100 candidates, averaged over queries

eval.protocol: single reported score per cell, no significance test or variance; Banking and SemEval15 scores use de-duplicated inputs/answers

availability.data: github.com/PolyAI-LDN/conversational-datasets (Reddit, OpenSubtitles, AmazonQA, Ubuntu); Banking dataset release not stated

evidence.quote: decaying the learning rate by 0.3x every 1M training steps after the ﬁrst 2.5M steps

results.claim: FT-DIRECT beats TARGET-ONLY on Ubuntu by a large margin (from-scratch overfits)
results.setup: R100@1 x100%, 100 candidates, one relevant; Reddit-pretrained input-response encoder; Ubuntu test, FT-DIRECT vs TARGET-ONLY
R100@1 x100%, 100 candidates, one relevant; Reddit-pretrained input-response encoder; BANKING test (1,485 pairs), FT-DIRECT
results.table: Table 3, row FT-DIRECT, column BANKING (TARGET-ONLY 88.3, REDDIT-DIRECT 27.3)

results.claim: FT-DIRECT on SemEval15 is below FT-MIXED; both far above TARGET-ONLY
results.setup: R100@1 x100%, 100 candidates, one relevant; Reddit-pretrained input-response encoder; SEMEVAL15, FT-DIRECT (FT-MIXED 56.5, TARGET-ONLY 7.5, USE-LARGE-MAP 56.5)
results.note: USE-LARGE-MAP also scores 56.5, equal to FT-MIXED; paper says gains for all domains but SEMEVAL15.

results.setup: R100@1 x100%, 100 candidates, one relevant; Reddit-pretrained input-response encoder; AMAZONQA, FT-DIRECT

results.claim: FT-DIRECT on OpenSubtitles, slight gain over scratch
results.setup: R100@1 x100%, 100 candidates, one relevant; Reddit-pretrained input-response encoder; OPENSUB, FT-DIRECT

results.setup: Reddit held-out 50K pairs; full model, Table 2

results.setup: Reddit test; cumulative ablation (each row removes a further component)

results.claim: Gain of FT-DIRECT over REDDIT-DIRECT on Banking
results.note: Printed as %, but they are absolute points. Ubuntu 38.7-9.6=29.1, not 32.5 (32.5 equals 38.7-6.2, the gain over TARGET-ONLY). Other three check out.
results.quote: the gains over REDDIT-DIRECT are +67.5% on BANKING, +32.5% on UBUNTU, +22.8% on AMAZONQA, and +11.5% on OPEN-

results.claim: FT-MIXED keeps Reddit performance while FT-DIRECT degrades on it
results.setup: Reddit test after fine-tuning on Banking with FT-MIXED (FT-DIRECT 55.3, TARGET-ONLY 1.2)
results.note: FT-MIXED Reddit scores 59.4-60.0 across domains; FT-DIRECT falls to 30.8-55.3.
results.table: Table 3, row FT-MIXED, column BANKING parenthesis

results.claim: Pretrain once on Reddit takes about 18 hours on 13 K80 nodes; fine-tuning takes minutes
results.setup: 13 GPU nodes, one Tesla K80 each; ~2B examples seen
results.quote: we train the model on 13 GPU nodes with one Tesla K80 each for 18 hours: the model sees around 2B examples

results.claim: Off-the-shelf encoders without a response mapping do poorly vs TF-IDF
results.setup: USE-SIM on Ubuntu vs TF-IDF 27.5 and BM25 19.6

results.claim: Approximate NN search speedup on Reddit test
results.setup: Malkov and Yashunin HNSW, 95% top-30 recall
results.quote: experiments on Reddit test data reveal a 130× speed-up using the approximate search method of Malkov and Yashunin (2016) while retaining 95% top-30 recall

limits: Only 5 domains are fine-tuned; Reddit is held out, though 'six target domains' appears in abstract/Table 3 caption and conclusion says five.
Single scores, no seeds or significance tests.
Fine-tuning hyperparameters (lr, batch, steps) not stated; no code or weights released.
Random negatives only; harder negative sampling left to future work.
Compared with BERT/USE only as frozen encoders, not fine-tuned for response selection.
Supplemental t-SNE for all 77 categories not in PDF.
